title: How Do You Defend Against AI That Can Hack?

reader_summary.headline: Security tools fail against AI agents because they were built for malware and humans.
reader_summary.overview: Current security defenses cannot stop AI attackers because these agents do not use malware or act like humans. Traditional methods like static rules and honey pots fail when autonomous agents find hidden credentials. Defenders must use flexible tools that can switch between models when one refuses to help.

key_points.text: Existing security tools were built for malware and humans, but AI agents are neither of those things.
key_points.evidence_quote: The challenge with the existing security tools that are out there is they really were built to tackle two things. The first thing people in the second is malware and AI and AI incident genetic processes are neither one of those things.

key_points.text: Old defenses fail because autonomous agents can find hidden credentials to bypass static detection rules and honey pots.
